A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BBQ research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, the IHQ user study, bootstrap analyses, and controlled uncertainty-calibration simulations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and simulations and adds prior-sensitivity results in Appendix C, Tables 2–5.

M1.justification: The core mixture model, priors, and EM parameter updates remain unchanged. Section 5 newly sketches an input adaptation that converts ranked lists into weighted pairwise comparisons before applying BBQ. This is a proposed extension, without reported implementation or evaluation.

E1.justification: The specified coverage remains HUMAINE, MT-Bench, WD, HiFiC, ConHa, the three IHQ variants, and the equal-skill simulation. Dataset descriptions partly move from the appendix into Section 4. Prior sweeps reuse existing datasets; ranked-list and active-selection applications are only discussed.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark comparisons retain Bayes-BT, attributed to Caron and Doucet, and the Google Research implementation labeled Crowd-BT, attributed to Chen et al. Newly discussed ranking methods are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4 replaces full-dataset reference rankings for HUMAINE and IHQ with the public HUMAINE and official CLIC leaderboards. Top-1 and Kendall’s tau therefore measure agreement against different references for these datasets. Appendix C also introduces controlled Gamma- and Beta-prior parameter sweeps; the main experiments retain their default priors and stopping threshold.

E4.justification: New Appendix C and Tables 2–5 test sensitivity to Gamma shape/rate for Bayes-BT and BBQ and Beta parameters for BBQ on IHQ-all and ConHa. This adds a substantial investigation of dependence on prior choices. Existing rater-count, comparisons-per-rater, rater-quality, and uncertainty-calibration analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 10,000 rater bootstrap resamples, reduced to 1,000 for HUMAINE, and 10,000 calibration trials with 50 comparisons per rater. The 99% interval procedures remain unchanged. Moving these details into the main text and adding prior-sensitivity scores does not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces HUMAINE and IHQ results under revised reference rankings: BBQ’s HUMAINE top-1/tau values change from 97.50%/0.9463 to 98.50%/0.9025, which is not a same-setting performance comparison. BBQ changes from second to third on IHQ-screened tau; v2 reports 0.9204 versus Crowd-BT’s 0.9238 and Bayes-BT’s 0.9211. Tables 2–5 add extensive prior-sensitivity outcomes.

T1.justification: Equation 10 and the derivation, moved from Appendix B to A, revise the complete-data factorization. v2 corrects the sign of the random-choice log-2 term and restores missing sums over raters in the expected likelihood and Q-function. It also adds explicit conditioning and independence statements. The final EM updates are retained.

C1.justification: The principal contribution remains Bayesian joint estimation of item skills and rater quality through closed-form EM updates. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion narrow comparative speed claims from faster or rapid convergence to efficient inference and competitive runtime. Evaluation claims also shift toward agreement with specified reference rankings.

C2.justification: Section 5 replaces the pairwise-only limitation with ranked-list and active-selection possibilities and removes the limited-bootstrap caveat. Appendix F newly explains that the equal-skill simulation isolates null calibration rather than real-world heterogeneity. Appendix E argues that short sessions limit attention drift, while Appendix B adds an interpretation of robustness across prior choices.

D1.justification: v2 documents the prior-sweep grids and fixed parameters, identifies the leaderboard references, and newly discloses that user-study sessions typically lasted under about ten minutes. The original implementation descriptions, default hyperparameters, stopping criterion, and dataset access remain. The session information is additional disclosure, not evidence that the study procedure changed.

R1.justification: Related work adds positioning against spectral, robust, and approximate ranking approaches, citing Oh, Shah and Wainwright, and Heckel et al. Discussion adds rank-breaking and Thompson-sampling references. The central novelty positioning against existing Bayesian BT and rater-quality models remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted explanatory rewrites, moves dataset and bootstrap descriptions into Section 4, and changes Limitations to Discussion. It removes the LLM-use appendix and adds conflict-of-interest and impact statements. The main section sequence and much of the existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from single-column to two-column formatting, with substantial resizing and repositioning of figures and equations. The calibration plot moves from appendix Figure 6 to main-text Figure 4. Four new multi-part sensitivity tables are added, while the dataset table and user-study images are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The prior-sensitivity experiments, explicitly sourced reference rankings, and derivation corrections improve the paper’s empirical support and mathematical presentation. The new conflict-of-interest disclosure also improves transparency. These gains are qualified by unreconciled reporting: Section 4.1 and Table 1’s caption still describe BBQ as second on IHQ-screened, although the revised tau values place it third. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
